Use Sylow counting on the 7-Sylow subgroups. The order is \(56 = 2^3\cdot 7\), so for \(p=7\), the number \(n_7 := \#\mathrm{Sylow}_7(G)\) both divides \(56/7=8\) and satisfies \(n_7 \equiv 1 \pmod 7\). The only positive divisor of \(8\) congruent to \(1\) mod \(7\) is \(1\). Hence there is a unique Sylow 7-subgroup, so it is normal. A simple group cannot have a nontrivial proper normal subgroup; but a Sylow 7-subgroup has order \(7\), so it is neither trivial nor the whole group (since \(7 \ne 1,56\)). Contradiction.
